hook.situation: You are reacting in real time: Korean feels more fun than expected, someone has already arrived, a friend may be late, and a missed plan still feels disappointing. The grammar is in the ending because the ending tells the listener how you are taking the information.
objectives: Use -네요 for fresh realization from what you just noticed.
Use -군요/-구나 for stronger acknowledgement or exclamation.
Use -(으)ㄹ걸요 for a softened prediction and -았/었을 텐데요 for regret or unfulfilled expectation.
hook.whyItMatters: A plain statement reports information. These endings report your stance toward the information. 재미있어요, 재미있네요, and 재미있군요 can describe the same fact, but they do not sound like the same reaction.

grammarNotes.title: A/V-네요: I just noticed this
grammarNotes.mentalModel: -네요 puts the listener beside you at the moment of discovery. You are reacting to something you just saw, heard, felt, or realized.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -네요 to the predicate stem. Past realization uses -았/었네요: 왔네요, 도착했네요, 재미있네요.

examples.en: Korean is more fun than I expected.
examples.note: The speaker is freshly realizing it while studying.

examples.en: It is not as hard as I thought.
examples.note: Good after trying something and changing your first impression.

exceptions: Do not use -네요 for information you have known all along. It can sound oddly performative.
-네요 is softer and more conversational than -군요.

grammarNotes.title: A/V-군요 and -구나: I see, so that is the case
grammarNotes.mentalModel: -군요 sounds like a more deliberate acknowledgement or exclamation. -구나 is casual and often used to oneself or with close people.
grammarNotes.formation: Adjective/copula stem + 군요. Present action verb + 는군요. Casual form: -구나.

examples.note: Polite acknowledgement after learning the fact.

examples.ko: 처음에는 어려울 줄 알았는데 생각보다 괜찮군요.
examples.romanization: cheoeumeneun eoryeoul jul aranneunde saenggakboda gwaenchanhgunyo.
examples.en: I thought it would be hard at first, but it is better than expected.
examples.note: A slightly formal realization, not just a casual comment.
-구나 is casual, suitable with close friends or self-talk.

exceptions: For action verbs in present tense, use -는군요: 잘하는군요, 오는군요.
-구나 can sound too casual or teacher-like if used to someone you are not close to.

grammarNotes.title: V-(으)ㄹ걸요: probably, I would guess
grammarNotes.mentalModel: -ㄹ걸요 lets you make a confident guess without sounding too blunt. It often feels like "I think probably..."
grammarNotes.formation: Verb/adjective stem + -(으)ㄹ걸요. Past guess uses -았/었을걸요: 이미 알았을걸요.

examples.en: If you leave now, you will probably be a little late.
examples.note: A softened prediction, not a command.
The speaker is fairly confident but leaves room.

examples.en: It will probably be crowded because it is the weekend.

exceptions: For personal regret, learners often hear the related form -ㄹ걸 그랬어요: 미리 말할걸 그랬어요.
-ㄹ걸요 is not the same as -겠어요. -ㄹ걸요 sounds like a hedged assertion to the listener.

grammarNotes.title: V-았/었을 텐데요: it would have happened, but it did not
grammarNotes.mentalModel: -았/었을 텐데요 looks back at a missed condition or expectation. It often carries a soft regret instead of a direct complaint.
grammarNotes.formation: Past stem + -았/었을 텐데요. It often follows a condition with -았/었으면.

examples.ko: 어제 시간이 있었으면 같이 갔을 텐데요.
examples.romanization: eoje sigani isseosseumyeon gachi gasseul tendeyo.
examples.en: If I had had time yesterday, I would have gone with you.
examples.note: The event did not happen; the ending keeps the regret soft.

examples.en: If I had known in advance, I would have helped.
examples.note: Polite regret after missing a chance to help.

examples.ko: 조금 더 연습했으면 훨씬 쉬웠을 텐데요.
examples.romanization: jogeum deo yeonseupaesseumyeon hwolssin swiwosseul tendeyo.
examples.en: If I had practiced a little more, it would have been much easier.

exceptions: Present/future -(으)ㄹ 텐데 is a guess or concern. Past -았/었을 텐데 is the regret/unfulfilled expectation frame.
If you need a direct apology, add an apology. -을 텐데요 alone only implies regret.

grammarNotes.title: -군요 vs -네요: both realize, but differently
grammarNotes.mentalModel: -네요 is immediate and conversational. -군요 is more formal, reflective, or exclamatory.
grammarNotes.formation: Use -네요 for fresh noticing. Use -군요/-구나 when acknowledging or exclaiming after information settles.

examples.ko: 연습을 많이 했으니까 잘하는 게 당연하네요.
examples.romanization: yeonseubeul mani haesseunikka jalhaneun ge dangyeonhaneyo.
examples.en: Since you practiced a lot, no wonder you are good.
examples.note: -네요 frames 당연하다 as a fresh realization.

examples.en: Oh, so that was the reason.

examples.note: 군요 accepts the new fact; 네요 marks the speaker's own realization.

exceptions: 그렇네요 is also natural, but it sounds more like you are agreeing after seeing/realizing it yourself.
그렇군요 is a common polite backchannel meaning "I see."

exampleSentence.en: Korean is more fun than I expected.
It is not as hard as I thought.
exampleSentence.note: This word naturally triggers realization endings because expectation changed.

exampleSentence.ko: 처음에는 어려울 줄 알았는데 생각보다 괜찮군요.
exampleSentence.en: I thought it would be hard at first, but it is better than expected.
exampleSentence.note: 어려울 줄 알았다 sets the old expectation.
벌써 pairs well with surprise or realization.
Past honorific 도착하셨군요 fits polite acknowledgement.

exampleSentence.en: If you leave now, you will probably be a little late.
If I had had time, I would have gone with you.
exampleSentence.note: 시간이 있었으면 creates the missed condition.

exampleSentence.en: I would have gone together with you.
exampleSentence.note: 같이 makes the regret relational, not just logistical.
이미 often appears in hedged assertions.

exampleSentence.en: There are more people than expected.
It probably is not certain yet.
If I had said it clearly, there would have been no misunderstanding.
exampleSentence.note: 분명히 sharpens the missed action in a regret sentence.

extendedVocabulary.english: to be natural, obvious, no wonder

exampleSentence.ko: 연습을 많이 했으니까 잘하는 게 당연하네요.
exampleSentence.en: Since you practiced a lot, no wonder you are good.
exampleSentence.note: -네요 makes the comment a realization, not a dismissive judgment.

exampleSentence.en: That must have been really hard for you.
exampleSentence.note: -군요 can acknowledge someone else's experience with empathy.
알고 있을걸요 is a common hedged assertion.

exampleSentence.en: I see. I did not know that.
exampleSentence.note: 군요 accepts the fact; 네요 marks the speaker's realization.

extendedDialogue.setting: Friends react to a class, a late schedule, and a missed chance while choosing endings that match their stance.

readingText.title: 끝 어미가 태도를 바꾼다
readingText.body: 민서는 첫 수업을 듣고 "생각보다 재미있네요"라고 말했다. 방금 느낀 놀라움이라서 -네요가 자연스러웠다. 지훈은 설명을 듣고 "그렇군요"라고 했다. 새 정보를 받아들이는 조금 더 차분한 반응이었다. 수업이 끝난 뒤 선생님이 이미 도착한 것을 보고 민서는 "벌써 도착하셨네요"라고 했고, 지훈은 시간을 보더니 "지금 출발하면 늦을걸요"라고 했다. 나중에 민서는 약속에 가지 못한 일을 떠올리며 "시간이 있었으면 같이 갔을 텐데요"라고 말했다. 같은 사실도 끝 어미가 달라지면 놀람, 인정, 예측, 아쉬움이 서로 다르게 들린다.
readingText.bodyTranslation: After the first class, Minseo said, "It is more fun than I expected." Because it was a surprise she had just felt, -네요 was natural. Jihoon listened to an explanation and said, "I see." That was a calmer acknowledgement of new information. After class, Minseo saw that the teacher had already arrived and said, "Oh, the teacher has already arrived." Jihoon looked at the time and said, "If we leave now, we will probably be late." Later, Minseo remembered not being able to go to an appointment and said, "If I had had time, I would have gone with you." Even with the same facts, the final ending changes whether the sentence sounds like surprise, acknowledgement, prediction, or regret.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 민서는 첫 수업 뒤에 어떤 어미를 사용했어요?
지훈이 "늦을걸요"라고 한 이유는 무엇이에요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 지금 출발하면 늦을 것 같다고 부드럽게 예측했기 때문이에요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: -았/었을 텐데요는 어떤 느낌을 나타냈어요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 과거에 이루어지지 않은 일에 대한 아쉬움이나 후회를 나타냈어요.

culturalNote.title: 끝 어미는 목소리의 표정
culturalNote.body: In Korean, the final ending often carries the social expression that English might put in intonation. 재미있어요 reports a fact. 재미있네요 shares a fresh reaction. 재미있군요 sounds like a more formal acknowledgement. 늦을걸요 warns softly without sounding bossy. 갔을 텐데요 lets regret trail off instead of making a heavy complaint.
culturalNote.tip: Before choosing the ending, ask: am I noticing, acknowledging, guessing, or regretting?

bullets: -네요 marks a fresh realization: 생각보다 재미있네요, 벌써 도착하셨네요.
-군요/-구나 marks stronger acknowledgement or exclamation: 그렇군요, 알고 있었구나.
-(으)ㄹ걸요 softens a prediction or assertion: 늦을걸요, 이미 알고 있을걸요.
-았/었을 텐데요 looks back at an unfulfilled past expectation: 같이 갔을 텐데요.
